items.physical_scope: A definition of gauge-fixed fluctuation and finite-regulator data for Euclidean rigid supersymmetry. It asserts no arbitrary-background existence, ellipticity, determinant evaluation, finite-dimensional regulator existence, continuum measure, regulator-removal theorem, or empirical conclusion.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $M$ be a compact oriented smooth four-manifold with a Riemannian metric and with the spin, gauge, matter, auxiliary, and R-symmetry bundles supplied as part of a rigid-background package. For each declared field species $a$, let $E_a\to M$ be its specified vector bundle. Assign each species a parity $p(a)\in\{\bar 0,\bar 1\}$, including a separate parity for every auxiliary and ghost species, and put $E^{\bar j}=\bigoplus_{p(a)=\bar j}E_a$. Physical bosons are even and physical fermions are odd; ghosts may have either declared parity. The grading is parity modulo two. Write $\Gamma^\infty(M,E)$ for the space of smooth sections of a bundle $E\to M$, with the topology of uniform convergence of every covariant derivative. A connection is an affine variable, represented by its difference from a fixed reference connection, an adjoint-valued one-form. Smooth sections are the common classical domain unless a different domain is stated.

For linearization, supply a local graded field chart at the chosen configuration $\Phi_*$. Its even coordinates range over an open neighborhood of zero in a specified closed real linear subspace $V^{\bar 0}$ of the even section space; its odd coordinates are formal anticommuting variables with values in a specified closed linear subspace $V^{\bar 1}$ of the odd section space. Complex fields may be regarded as real pairs, with a declared complexification when required by $Q$. In this chart $\Phi_*$ has coordinate zero and the tangent fluctuations are $V=V^{\bar 0}\oplus V^{\bar 1}$. Require the chart, its inverse onto its image, and the coefficient maps of $Q$ to be smooth: all iterated directional derivatives in the even variables exist and are jointly continuous in the base point and directions; dependence on odd variables is specified by continuous alternating multilinear coefficient maps, smooth in the even variables. Taylor expansions below are formal jets at zero, with no convergence assertion. Products obey $uv=(-1)^{|u||v|}vu$ for homogeneous variables, and $Q$ obeys $Q(uv)=(Qu)v+(-1)^{|u|}u(Qv)$. Reality, contour, gauge, and boundary constraints used to restrict this chart must have a supplied smooth parametrization and be preserved by $Q$ (or by its declared complexification). Their tangent space is the image of the chart derivative, with the corresponding linearized conditions; it is not inferred from an arbitrary subset of sections. Gauge fixing by an action insertion does not by itself restrict the fields to a gauge slice. No smooth chart, or tangency to a contour or slice, is asserted to follow merely from specifying those conditions.

A gauge-fixed supersymmetry fluctuation datum at a smooth $Q$-fixed configuration $\Phi_*$, meaning a configuration with $Q\Phi_*=0$ after the declared gauge fixing, consists of the field bundles, the declared gauge-fixing condition, its Faddeev–Popov operator, the ghost and auxiliary fields, and the odd gauge-fixed transformation $Q$ on every field. Here $Q$ is the sum of the selected off-shell supersymmetry transformation and the specified gauge-fixing or BRST differential. Its square $H=Q^2$ is part of the data and must be given on every field; it may be a nonzero combination of gauge, spacetime, R-symmetry, and flavor transformations. For the round-sphere model used in this page, take the fields, spinors, gamma matrices, bundle lifts, ghost domains and gauge fermion from the adopted rigid N=4 Yang–Mills localization background on the round four-sphere postulate. Its total gauge-fixed convention is $Q=s+\delta$ and $H=\delta_{\rm gauge}(a_0)+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)$ on fields and ghosts, with $\delta_{\rm gauge}(u)A_\mu=-D_\mu u$ on the connection and $\delta_{\rm gauge}(u)X=[u,X]$ on adjoint tensors. Here $\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)=-\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}-\delta_R$ is the combined geometric-lift/R operator, with $R^Q_{AB}=2\epsilon\widetilde\Gamma_{AB}\widetilde\epsilon$ in the source order and the auxiliary-index lift fixed by its off-shell square; its action on adjoint ghosts is $-\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}$. The lift is separate from the gauge-covariant source Lie derivative: in a local gauge frame with lift coefficient $\beta_{v,P}$, the latter is $\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}+\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\kappa_v)$ with $\kappa_v=v^\mu A_\mu-\beta_{v,P}+v^A\Phi_A$. The unpaired parameter is $\phi=-\kappa_v$, with affine ghost rule $\delta\phi=-[c,\phi]+\rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega)c$; $a_0$ lies in the fixed background stabilizer algebra $\ker D_{A_*}$. The declared sectorwise background-gauge insertion is the completed $Q\Psi_{\mathrm{gf}}$ on its specified ghost/zero-mode domains. Thus $Q$ is not called nilpotent unless $H$ acts as zero on the specified sector.

In the supplied chart write $\eta=\Phi-\Phi_*$ for the fluctuation coordinates and expand the field transformation as $Q\eta=\mathcal D_{\Phi_*}\eta+O(\eta^2)$, where $O(\eta^2)$ means terms of total Taylor degree at least two in even and odd fluctuations. The zero-degree term vanishes by $Q\Phi_*=0$. This defines $\mathcal D_{\Phi_*}=(dQ)_{\Phi_*}$ as the odd linearized field transformation on $V$, extended to products by the graded Leibniz rule. The square $Q^2$ means composition as a derivation on fields, equivalently $\tfrac12[Q,Q]$ with the graded commutator. Since $Q$ has no constant term, it preserves terms of degree at least two; taking the linear part of $Q^2\eta=H\eta$ therefore gives $\mathcal D_{\Phi_*}^2=(dH)_{\Phi_*}$. On the common smooth domain $V$, $\mathcal D_{\Phi_*}$ preserves $\ker(dH)_{\Phi_*}$ because it commutes with its own square. Its restriction there is a parity-graded cochain differential, meaning an odd linear map with square zero. If the chart is affine in the fields and $Q$ is a finite-order differential transformation with smooth dependence on finitely many field derivatives, $\mathcal D_{\Phi_*}$ is a matrix of finite-order differential operators. For operator domains on a compact manifold, one may choose Sobolev completions $W^{k,2}(M,E_a)$ defined by requiring all weak covariant derivatives through order $k$ to be square-integrable with respect to the chosen metric and bundle metric. An operator of order $m$ then maps $W^{k,2}$ to $W^{k-m,2}$ for a declared integer $k\ge m$; the bundle metrics, connections, boundary conditions, and closed-operator realization are additional data. Compositions of closed realizations require their own common domain; the square identity above is on smooth fluctuations and does not assert equality of arbitrary closed extensions.

For a differential operator $D$ of order $m$, its principal symbol $\sigma_m(D)(x,\xi)$ is the homogeneous degree-$m$ part obtained in local coordinates by replacing each highest-order derivative $\partial_\mu$ by $i\xi_\mu$. A differential sequence is elliptic when its symbol sequence is exact for every nonzero cotangent vector $\xi$. For a specified smooth compact-group action on $M$, it is transversely elliptic when the symbol sequence is exact for every nonzero cotangent vector that annihilates the tangent space to the action orbit. Any claim of either property must identify the operators, symbols, domains, and symmetry directions; this definition asserts neither. A zero mode of $D$ is a vector in its specified domain that lies in $\ker D$. A Faddeev–Popov zero mode is a vector in the kernel of the specified Faddeev–Popov operator, and an infinitesimal gauge stabilizer is a gauge transformation that fixes the background connection. A one-loop determinant is a regularized determinant or ratio of determinants of specified fluctuation operators with their domains, spectra, phases, and zero-mode conventions fixed. A primed determinant omits only the stated kernel; the omitted modes require separate treatment. No determinant follows from the symbol or from a formal supercharge algebra alone.

A finite-dimensional regulator is extra data, not a consequence of the continuum fluctuation datum. It consists of a finite-dimensional oriented smooth field-parameter manifold $\mathfrak F_\rho$, a smooth positive volume form, an integration cycle and boundary conditions, a graded algebra identified with $\Omega^\bullet(\mathfrak F_\rho;\mathbb C)$, a graded integral of its top-degree part, and an odd derivation $Q_\rho$ induced by the declared field transformation. Its square is the induced symmetry $H_\rho$. In this page the finite-dimensional integration and deformation data use the exact conventions of the finite-dimensional Q-exact localization definition: $Q_\rho$-invariance means the integral of $Q_\rho F$ vanishes on the admissible integrands, including the zero-boundary-flux condition. This data does not identify the formal noncommutative S4 regulator with a finite-dimensional regulator, and it does not construct an infinite-dimensional field-space measure.

items.physical_scope: A conditional deduction for a fixed gauge-bundle sector of the source-qualified Euclidean N=4 SU(2) model on the round S4, only after a separately supplied finite-dimensional Q-preserving regulator satisfies the stated hypotheses. It proves neither that such a regulator exists for the source's formal S4 construction nor a continuum measure, t-to-infinity saddle limit, regulator-removal theorem, or empirical claim.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and fix one bundle sector of the adopted massless $\mathcal N=4$ $SU(2)$ Yang–Mills model on the round Euclidean four-sphere $S^4_r$, with $r>0$ a length. The adopted background fixes the action, contour, field content, and total gauge-fixed odd transformation $Q=s+\delta$; on its fields and ghosts the square is $Q^2=\delta_{\rm gauge}(a_0)+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)$, where $a_0\in\mathfrak h_P=\ker D_{A_*}$ is the declared parallel background zero mode and $\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)=-\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}-\delta_R$ is the combined lifted spacetime/R action, not a second copy of a gauge-covariant Lie derivative. The nongauge action on ghosts is $\rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega)=-\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}$, and its auxiliary-index action is the one fixed by the source off-shell square. The source-ordered bilinear is $R^Q_{AB}=2\epsilon\widetilde\Gamma_{AB}\widetilde\epsilon$ and the cohomological parameter is $\phi=-(v^\mu A_\mu-\beta_{v,P}+v^A\Phi_A)$, where $\beta_{v,P}$ is the fixed lift's vertical coefficient. The adopted affine ghost rule is $\delta\phi=-[c,\phi]+\rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega)c$. Sectorwise gauge fixing is the $Q$-completed background-gauge insertion $Q\Psi_{\mathrm{gf}}$ with its specified ghost and zero-mode domains. This is a physical model assumption, not a deduction that the formal continuum functional integral exists.

For a fixed regulator label $\rho$, assume that a finite-dimensional regulator of this model is supplied by an oriented smooth field-parameter manifold $\mathfrak F_\rho$ of finite dimension $n$, a smooth positive volume form $\mu_\rho$, and integration over the whole cycle $\mathfrak F_\rho$. Let $\mathcal A_\rho=\Omega^\bullet(\mathfrak F_\rho;\mathbb C)$, let $I_\rho(F)=\int_{\mathfrak F_\rho}F_{[n]}$ be the integral of the degree-$n$ part, and let $Q_\rho$ be the induced smooth odd derivation. The regulator must preserve the stated total $Q$ action and its square; no regulator existence or regulator-preservation claim is assumed. Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval of dimensionless deformation parameters. Let $S_\rho,O_\rho\in\mathcal A_\rho$ be even, let $V_\rho\in\mathcal A_\rho$ be odd, and define $E_{\rho,t}=e^{-S_\rho-tQ_\rho V_\rho}$. In units with $\hbar=1$, assume the regulated action $S_\rho$ and deformation $tQ_\rho V_\rho$ are dimensionless. Assume $Q_\rho S_\rho=Q_\rho O_\rho=0$ and $(Q_\rho^2V_\rho)E_{\rho,t}=0$ for every $t\in J$. Assume the regulated measure and cycle are Q-invariant on the admissible integrands, in the exact sense that $I_\rho(Q_\rho(O_\rho V_\rho E_{\rho,t}))=0$ for every $t\in J$, with no anomaly or boundary contribution.

Write $(O_\rho E_{\rho,t})_{[n]}=f_{\rho,t}\mu_\rho$ and assume $f_{\rho,t}\in L^1(\mathfrak F_\rho,\mu_\rho)$ for every $t\in J$. Assume there is a measurable $\mu_\rho$-null set $N_\rho\subseteq\mathfrak F_\rho$ such that, for every $x\in\mathfrak F_\rho\setminus N_\rho$, the map $t\mapsto f_{\rho,t}(x)$ is differentiable at every $t\in J$. For $x\notin N_\rho$ define

$$\partial_t f_{\rho,t}(x):=\lim_{\substack{h\to0\\h\in\mathbb R,\ h\ne0,\ t+h\in J}}\frac{f_{\rho,t+h}(x)-f_{\rho,t}(x)}{h}\in\mathbb C,$$

and define $\partial_t f_{\rho,t}(x)=0$ for $x\in N_\rho$. Require $x\mapsto\partial_t f_{\rho,t}(x)$ to be measurable for every $t\in J$. For every compact $K\subset J$, assume one nonnegative $g_K\in L^1(\mathfrak F_\rho,\mu_\rho)$ and one $\mu_\rho$-null set $N_{\rho,K}$ such that, for every $x\notin N_{\rho,K}$ and every $t\in K$,

$$|f_{\rho,t}(x)|\le g_K(x),\qquad |\partial_t f_{\rho,t}(x)|\le g_K(x).$$

Then

$$Z_\rho(t):=I_\rho(O_\rho E_{\rho,t})$$

is constant on $J$, and for every $t\in J$,

$$Z_\rho'(t)=-I_\rho(O_\rho(Q_\rho V_\rho)E_{\rho,t})=-I_\rho(Q_\rho(O_\rho V_\rho E_{\rho,t}))=0.$$

The conclusion applies only to this fixed finite-dimensional regulator and fixed bundle sector at finite $t$. The adopted S4 postulate does not construct the finite-dimensional data above, and this result supplies no infinite-dimensional continuum identity, $t\to\infty$ localization limit, or regulator-removal theorem.

items.title: A finite Q-exact torus integral with constant value
items.physical_scope: A dimensionless finite-dimensional graded integral used only as an illustration of the Ward identity; it is not identified with the S4 field configuration space and gives no continuum or empirical prediction.
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^2/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^2$ be the two-torus with dimensionless angular coordinates $x,y$ modulo $2\pi$; $dx,dy$ denote the induced global angular one-forms. Orient $M$ by the volume form $\mu=dx\wedge dy$ and define the graded integral $I(F)=\int_M F_{[2]}$.

The complex differential-form algebra is $\Omega^\bullet(M;\mathbb C)=\Omega^0\oplus\Omega^1\oplus\Omega^2$, where $C^\infty(M;\mathbb C)$ is the space of smooth functions periodic in both coordinates, $\Omega^0=C^\infty(M;\mathbb C)$, $\Omega^1=\{a\,dx+b\,dy:a,b\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb C)\}$, $\Omega^2=\{c\,dx\wedge dy:c\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb C)\}$, and $\Omega^k=0$ for $k>2$. The product is the exterior product, determined by $dx\wedge dx=dy\wedge dy=0$ and $dy\wedge dx=-dx\wedge dy$. The exterior derivative is the degree-one linear map $d$ defined by $df=(\partial_x f)dx+(\partial_y f)dy$, $d(a\,dx+b\,dy)=(\partial_x b-\partial_y a)dx\wedge dy$, and $d\alpha=0$ for $\alpha\in\Omega^2$; these formulas give the graded Leibniz rule and $d^2=0$.

Let the odd derivation be $Q=d$, set the dimensionless action $S=0$, choose the even insertion $O=1+\lambda\,dx\wedge dy$ for $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, and choose the odd deformation $V=\sin(x)\,dy$. For every dimensionless real $t$, the integral $Z(t)=I(Oe^{-S-tQV})$ equals $4\pi^2\lambda$. This is a finite-dimensional regulator toy integral only; it is not a model of the S4 field configuration space or a continuum physical prediction.

items.title: A Q-exact deformation with a nonzero boundary term
items.physical_scope: A finite-dimensional graded integral on a compact manifold with boundary, included only to exhibit the boundary obstruction; it is not an S4 field theory, empirical result, or continuum claim.
items.statement:
Let $M=[0,1]\times(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)$ be the cylinder as a smooth manifold with boundary, with dimensionless product coordinates $x,y$; $dx,dy$ denote the global product and angular one-forms. Orient $M$ by the volume form $dx\wedge dy$ and define the graded integral $I(F)=\int_M F_{[2]}$.

The complex differential-form algebra is $\Omega^\bullet(M;\mathbb C)=\Omega^0\oplus\Omega^1\oplus\Omega^2$, where $C^\infty(M;\mathbb C)$ is the space of functions smooth up to $x=0,1$ and periodic in $y$, $\Omega^0=C^\infty(M;\mathbb C)$, $\Omega^1=\{a\,dx+b\,dy:a,b\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb C)\}$, $\Omega^2=\{c\,dx\wedge dy:c\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb C)\}$, and $\Omega^k=0$ for $k>2$. The product is the exterior product, determined by $dx\wedge dx=dy\wedge dy=0$ and $dy\wedge dx=-dx\wedge dy$. The exterior derivative is the degree-one linear map $d$ defined by $df=(\partial_x f)dx+(\partial_y f)dy$, $d(a\,dx+b\,dy)=(\partial_x b-\partial_y a)dx\wedge dy$, and $d\alpha=0$ for $\alpha\in\Omega^2$; these formulas give the graded Leibniz rule and $d^2=0$.

Take the odd derivation $Q=d$, dimensionless action $S=0$, even insertion $O=1$, and odd deformation $V=x\,dy$. For every dimensionless real $t$, $Z(t)=I(Oe^{-S-tQV})=-2\pi t$. The change occurs because $I(Q(Ve^{-S-tQV}))=2\pi\ne0$: this cycle violates the zero-boundary Q-invariance condition and therefore is not an instance of the finite-dimensional Ward identity.
